Capture fixture window.scrollY: 0px

A deliberately long local page

This self-contained page gives the extension long text, embedded images, a canvas, fixed controls, and an independently scrollable region. Scroll partway down before capture to check that the page returns to the same position.

Opening notes

Each section adds enough content to require several viewport captures. The pale blue ridge below is an SVG image stored in a data URL, so the fixture makes no network requests.

A rendered-page capture keeps what Chrome paints. That means the fixed header and the floating button can repeat in a long image. This fixture makes that result visible instead of hiding it.

Embedded image blocks

The next image is also local. Its wide aspect ratio checks that adjacent viewports keep image pixels in order when the final viewport overlaps the previous one.

Long prose after the image creates a stable area for checking the end of one frame and the start of another. The same words appear only once in the document, so duplicated or missing rows are easy to spot in a saved PNG.

Canvas chart

The chart is drawn at page load. It exercises the canvas pixels that a DOM-only capture would often miss.

Capture this section at a point where the chart crosses a viewport boundary. The axes, bars, and line should remain continuous in the downloaded file.

Nested scrolling

This panel scrolls independently from the document. Move its scrollbar before capture if you want to compare its visible state in the output.

Nested entry 1. The page scroll position must not change while this box scrolls.

Nested entry 2. The extension captures the visible viewport, including this element.

Nested entry 3. A capture does not try to stitch the box's off-screen contents.

Nested entry 4. The final entry makes the internal scrollbar long enough to use.

Closing section

This last section helps produce a partial final viewport on common desktop window sizes. The green landscape is the final embedded image. After a capture, compare the fixed readout with the position you set before starting.

End of fixture. The extra paragraph leaves a short tail below the image so the final capture includes both image pixels and text.
